title: Light Speed
text: Light travels at approximately 299,792 kilometers per second in a vacuum. It takes about 8 minutes for light to travel from the Sun to Earth.

title: Mars Atmosphere
text: Mars has a very thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide (95%), with traces of nitrogen and argon. The atmospheric pressure is less than 1% of Earth's.

title: Black Holes
text: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it passes the event horizon.

title: Water on Earth
text: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water. However, only about 2.5% of all water on Earth is freshwater, and less than 1% is easily accessible.

title: Human DNA
text: Human DNA is approximately 99.9% identical between any two individuals. The remaining 0.1% accounts for all genetic variation among humans.

title: Moon Formation
text: The Moon formed approximately 4.5 billion years ago, likely from debris after a Mars-sized body collided with early Earth.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth at 8,849 meters above sea level. It grows about 4 millimeters per year due to tectonic activity.

title: Ocean Depth
text: The Mariana Trench is the deepest part of the ocean, reaching depths of approximately 11,034 meters. Pressure at the bottom is over 1,000 times atmospheric pressure.

title: Antarctica
text: Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent. It contains about 90% of the world's ice and 70% of its freshwater.

title: Human Heart
text: The human heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping approximately 7,500 liters of blood. It creates enough pressure to squirt blood 30 feet.

title: Earth's Core
text: Earth's inner core is a solid ball of iron-nickel alloy about 2,400 kilometers in diameter, with temperatures reaching 5,700 C - similar to the Sun's surface.

title: Volcanoes
text: There are approximately 1,500 active volcanoes on Earth. About 50 of these erupt each year, while about 20 are actively erupting at any given time.

title: Human Brain
text: The human brain contains about 86 billion neurons and uses about 20% of the body's total energy, despite being only 2% of body weight.

title: Rainbow Formation
text: Rainbows form when sunlight is refracted, reflected, and dispersed in water droplets, creating a spectrum of light with red on the outer edge and violet on the inner edge.

title: Earth's Rotation
text: Earth rotates on its axis once every 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds. This rotation is gradually slowing due to tidal friction.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy, producing oxygen and glucose. Plants produce about 70% of Earth's oxygen through this process.

title: Earth's Magnetic Field
text: Earth's magnetic field extends thousands of kilometers into space and protects the planet from solar wind and cosmic radiation.

title: Human Lungs
text: Human lungs contain about 300 million alveoli, providing a surface area of roughly 70 square meters for gas exchange.

title: Tsunamis
text: Tsunamis are giant waves caused by underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides. They can travel at speeds up to 800 kilometers per hour.

title: Auroras
text: Auroras (Northern and Southern Lights) occur when charged particles from the solar wind interact with Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere.

title: Desert Formation
text: Deserts cover about one-third of Earth's land surface. They form due to atmospheric circulation patterns, mountain rain shadows, or cold ocean currents.

title: Human Blood
text: Human blood contains about 5 liters of fluid with red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma. Red blood cells live about 120 days.

title: Earth's Age
text: Earth is approximately 4.54 billion years old, based on radiometric dating of meteorites and Earth's oldest rocks.

title: Coral Reefs
text: Coral reefs cover less than 0.1% of the ocean floor but support about 25% of all marine species.

title: Earth's Atmosphere
text: Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases, extending about 480 kilometers above the surface.
